speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We require them to comply with our road traffic laws and regulations, and we conduct on-road enforcement on them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Foreign vehicles that commit speeding offences will be dealt with in accordance with the law.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We do not require them to install speed limiters, because they also ply in other jurisdictions with different speed limits from Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It is worth noting that, since Singapore-registered lorries are already required to install speed limiters and, therefore, will be unable to speed, this allows the Traffic Police to focus speeding enforcement on all other vehicles on our roads, including foreign-registered heavy vehicles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To Ms Joan Pereira’s question on installing speed limiters for "higher-risk passenger cars", speed limiters are currently required for heavy vehicles as part of a targeted, risk-based approach.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These vehicles pose higher risks due to their size, weight and operating characteristics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: But the risks associated with passenger cars, on the other hand, arise primarily from driver behaviour, rather than vehicle attributes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These behaviours are more appropriately addressed through public education efforts and deterrent penalties, rather than through speed limiters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Members also asked about speed limits for heavy vehicles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Ms Yeo Wan Ling asked whether the speed differential between passenger vehicles and heavy vehicles gives rise to unsafe driving conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Ms Valerie Lee suggested that lighter vehicles with a maximum laden weight of 3,501 to 5,000 kilogrammes should be subject to a higher speed limit of 70 kilometres per hour, instead of the current 60 kilometres per hour.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: On expressways, passenger vehicles may travel at speeds of up to 90 kilometres per hour, while heavy vehicles are subject to a vehicular speed limit of 60 kilometres per hour, enforced through speed limiters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: But these differing limits should not be seen in isolation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They are paired with lane-discipline requirements, where slower vehicles are required to keep to the left lane, except when overtaking.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The rationale for this framework is road safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Heavy vehicles differ from passenger vehicles in terms of mass, braking distance, stability and blind spots; and when accidents occur, they can cause disproportionate harm.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Speed control is, therefore, a critical safety lever to reduce the risk and severity of accidents involving such vehicles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To Ms Valerie Lee's suggestion, vehicles with a maximum laden weight of between 3,501 and 5,000 kilogrammes are subject to the same 60 kilometres per hour speed limit as vehicles above 5,000 kilogrammes because they pose similar road safety risks, such as longer braking distances and reduced manoeuvrability at higher speed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We expect these figures to further decrease after all lorries install speed limiters by 1 July 2027.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We also recognise that good lane discipline is essential where there are differences in vehicle speeds.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Traffic Police will continue to educate motorists on the importance of maintaining lane discipline and enforce against violations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Ms Yeo Wan Ling, Ms Valerie Lee and Dr Choo Pei Ling asked questions about the compliance burden on businesses and whether assistance is being provided to businesses to facilitate the installation of speed limiters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To Ms Yeo's query, the speed limiter requirement applies to lorries that continue to operate on Singapore roads.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Where a vehicle is earmarked to be scrapped after its statutory installation deadline, the vehicle must be installed with a speed limiter in order to operate on the roads after the deadline.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: While I appreciate Ms Yeo's suggestion to exercise flexibility for those with firm scrapping plans, we will have to draw the line somewhere and there will always be lorries which are intended to be scrapped after the deadline.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have thus decided to maintain a consistent approach by not extending the deadline for any group.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Lorry owners have been given adequate lead time to plan their installation decisions in accordance with their business and operational needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This recognises that speed limiters can also indirectly improve productivity by reducing downtime in the event of accidents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This expands the variety of approved speed limiters available in the market and provides more options for lorry owners looking to install speed limiters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The industry has also been offering on-site installation and bulk discounts to encourage installation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Turning to the other proposals in the Bill, Mr Jackson Lam asked how fairness and public trust would be maintained in the context of increasingly automated enforcement systems.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They also do not change the current process for appeals, including the viewing of camera footage upon request, which will continue to be managed by the Traffic Police.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These authorised civilians will assess traffic camera footage to determine if a traffic violation has been disclosed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is based on an assessment framework provided by Traffic Police.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, for footage captured by red light cameras, these civilians will view a series of photos to confirm that the vehicle had crossed the stop line after the traffic light had turned red.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In short, the authorised civilians will not exercise enforcement discretion.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Traffic Police will continue to be responsible and accountable for enforcement policy and decisions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are working out the procurement details and approach.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: That said, we agree with the Member that any use of automation or outsourcing must be subject to robust safeguards and oversight, to ensure fairness and public confidence in traffic enforcement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Ministry fully agrees with the need for adequate deterrence and appropriate punishment, commensurate with the culpability of the offender and the harm caused through the offending act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The maximum penalties set out in the Road Traffic Act reflect this calibrated approach.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Ministry is studying further measures to shape responsible driving behaviour and improve overall road safety.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Our intention is not to target any specific group, but to set ground rules that provide clarity and keep our paths safer for all.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: MOH has issued guidelines for healthcare professionals to conduct the assessment, including a non-exhaustive list of possible conditions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Some examples include cardiovascular diseases, such as severe heart failure; and musculoskeletal disorders, such as muscular dystrophies and rheumatoid arthritis.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Members including Mr David Hoe, Mr Ng Shi Xuan and Dr Hamid Razak asked about the process to obtain a Certificate of Medical Need, validity periods and timelines.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For the convenience of users and assessors, both digital and hard copy certificates will be possible.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The doctor or OT may fill in a standard online form to submit the data to LTA or issue a hard copy of the standard form.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Once the assessor completes the form, the certificate is granted.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For the hard copy, the user is encouraged to take a photo and submit it to LTA so that it is stored in LTA's digital registry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As part of the certification, the doctor or OT will assess and indicate if the user's need for a mobility scooter is long-term or temporary.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For the latter, the period that the Certificate is valid will be specified.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The Government will maintain a registry of those with valid Certificates of Medical Need and those exempted from the requirement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Seniors exempted on the basis of age will not be in the registry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I know some seniors may look younger than their age, so if enforcement officers were to ask, their National Registration Identity Card (NRIC) year of birth just needs to show that they are 70 years old and above.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As an example, for this year, everyone born in and before 1956 are automatically exempted.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Enforcement officers will request the user's particulars to perform a back-end check on the spot.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: If the certificate has not been submitted online, the user just needs to produce the hard copy form for inspection.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Individuals can also check their certification or exemption status on LTA's OneMotoring website.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Dr Choo Pei Ling asked whether physiotherapists can grant the Certificate of Medical Need.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We have worked with MOH to determine the groups of assessors for the certificate.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Currently, mobility assessment, device prescription and user training are not part of the routine training of a general physiotherapist.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Hence, MOH's position is that only doctors and OTs can assess and grant this certificate.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: MOH will continue to monitor demand if these competencies should be built into training for a wider pool of healthcare professionals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Members including Mr Jackson Lam and Mr Yip Hon Weng reminded us to streamline processes to minimise the burden on genuine users, particularly persons with disabilities and seniors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We are working to exempt more user groups with other relevant assessments where possible, such as applicants for other disability schemes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Members including Ms Yeo Wan Ling, Dr Wan Rizal and Ms Lee Hui Ying also asked about the cost to undergo the Assessment for Mobility Scooter (AMS), if polyclinics will offer the AMS and if subsidies will be extended.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For those who need certification, we have engaged the healthcare sector to encourage private GP clinics to offer the AMS.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We want it to be widely available and accessible, so that users can have affordable choices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As Dr Haresh Singaraju has emphasised, we encourage users to go to their regular doctor or regular OT, who already understand their medical history, to streamline the assessment process.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: All doctors, including polyclinic doctors, are allowed to conduct the AMS.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: However, doctors may decline to assess users who are not their regular patients, depending on the doctor's comfort level to conduct the certification.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: However, as long as the patient is seeking healthcare services from a doctor or OT at public healthcare institutions or community care organisations, and the AMS is conducted as a clinically indicated part of their regular medical care, the overall care episode, including the AMS, can be given healthcare subsidies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Members, including Mr Cai Yinzhou, Mr Dennis Tan and Mr David Hoe, asked about specific plans to engage existing PMA users on the new rules, especially seniors and persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: LTA will continue to work with the Agency for Integrated Care and SG Enable as well as relevant social service agencies, such as SPD, to reach out to seniors and persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: LTA's public communications campaign on the new rules will also be rolled out in various languages.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: On the ground, enforcement officers will engage and educate PMA users on the upcoming rules.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will also reach out through grassroots channels, and I seek Members' support to raise awareness among your residents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Members including Ms Yeo Wan Ling and Ms Joan Pereira raised concerns on how the new PMA rules may affect platform delivery workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We understand the concern on how the new rules could potentially affect the number of deliveries and thus the earnings of delivery workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Only workers with mobility needs should use PMAs for their work.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Such workers have to abide by the reduced speed limit and dimension limits for everyone's safety.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This protects not just other path users but the PMA riders themselves.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: By going at a slower speed and using devices that are not oversized, they can navigate crowded paths and complete their deliveries safely.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: They reduce the risks of serious accidents, which would affect their earning stability.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We had engaged the Digital Platforms Industry Association and the NDCA last year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: They expressed support for the new PMA rules, including the six kilometres an hour speed limit, in a joint statement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The platforms have committed to be inclusive in allocating jobs and providing earning opportunities for individuals from diverse backgrounds, including those with mobility challenges who rely on PMAs for their delivery work.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Ms Gho Sze Kee and Mr Yip Hon Weng also asked about platforms incentivising faster deliveries that may lead to speeding.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Platform companies are responsible for ensuring the safety and well-being of their delivery riders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This includes ensuring that their riders using active mobility devices on public paths have adequate third-party liability insurance coverage during the course of their work.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will continue to encourage food delivery platforms, rider associations and industry partners to promote safe riding practices and explore what more can be done to deter errant riding behaviour.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: LTA and the Traffic Police have also conducted campaigns, such as Be Safe, Be Seen, to promote safer riding habits with Grab, and safety talks and training sessions for delivery riders with foodpanda.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr David Hoe raised a concern that the reduced speed limit could affect users' ability to travel upslope.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Indeed, this was a concern that we had when developing the proposal.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: So, we spent some time studying the issue.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Our studies support the calculations done by Mr Hoe's volunteers – that motorised PMAs will be able to travel upslope along public paths safely with a speed limit of six kilometres per hour.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: It is the motor power and not the speed that pushes the wheels upslope.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Nonetheless, we understand the worries and LTA will improve awareness to reassure PMA users that six kilometres per hour is safe.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Ms He Ting Ru asked whether scientific literature was considered for the Active Mobility Advisory Panel's (AMAP's) recommendation of the speed limit reduction.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Ms Yeo Wan Ling, Mr Dennis Tan, Mr Fadli Fawzi and Mr Cai Yinzhou raised concerns that the lower speed limit would increase journey times and affect delivery riders' earnings.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We acknowledge that the trade-off is that users travel more slowly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This is necessary to protect themselves and other path users.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: So, I thank Mr Foo Cexiang for citing the many jurisdictions internationally that use six kilometres per hour as the speed limit for PMAs based on brisk walking speed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: On Ms He Ting Ru's suggestion, AMAP already comprises stakeholders across various interest and professional groups as well as academics.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Ms He Ting Ru and Mr Cai Yinzhou asked if users would have sufficient time to comply with the new rules that will come into effect on 1 June 2026.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We have received strong calls to implement the rules swiftly to improve path safety.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Foo Cexiang and Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about the cost of registration and how mobility scooters can be transferred or sold.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Retailers need to register the devices to their business before sale or ensure that the device is registered.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Ahead of 1 June 2026, LTA will work with retailers to register their existing stock of compliant mobility scooters.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Before the sale of the mobility scooter, retailers will check via OneMotoring website to ensure that the prospective owner is either granted a Certificate of Medical Need or exempted from the requirement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The sale should only be completed upon the successful transfer of ownership.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will be mindful that the cost of registration should be kept affordable so as not to place an undue burden on genuine users.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Dr Hamid Razak suggested markers to visibly identify those with medical need for mobility scooters for ease of enforcement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: On the other hand, Mr Foo Cexiang asked if registration and identification marks raised privacy concerns.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We appreciate these concerns and we assure Members that the registration and enforcement processes will be handled sensitively.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This is no different from how vehicles can be driven by multiple drivers as long as each driver has a valid driving licence and the vehicle is insured accordingly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Several Members, including Ms Tin Pei Ling, Ms Joan Pereira, Mr Dennis Tan and Mr David Hoe, raised suggestions to strengthen enforcement of the new PMA rules, including expanding the use of cameras, increasing plainclothes operations and action against non-compliant retailers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To enforce the PMA rules, LTA has a comprehensive strategy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Active Mobility Enforcement Officers will patrol public paths and conduct checks on user and device compliance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: They will be supported by volunteer Active Mobility Community Ambassadors to enhance engagement efforts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Ms He Ting Ru also expressed concern that enforcement officers will rely on casual visual perception of able-bodiedness.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Enforcement officers will be trained to be sensitive in checking for the Certificate of Medical Need.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Public tip-offs on errant users are gathered through LTA's website and social media today, as Members, such as Ms Poh Li San, Mr Ng Shi Xuan and Mr Cai Yin Zhou, have suggested.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These complement other data sources to identify offence hotspots for targeted enforcement deployments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Closed-circuit televisions (CCTVs) focused on paths are already deployed island-wide to detect and deter offences, such as speeding.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Some of the CCTVs are deployed permanently while others are deployed on a roving basis to allow us to respond quickly as new hotspots emerge.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In addition to ground enforcement, LTA conducts targeted operations against retailers who display or sell non-compliant and unregistered devices or offer illegal modification services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Non-compliant devices are seized and enforcement actions taken against offenders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: But we must acknowledge that no matter how many boots we put on the ground, enforcement officers cannot be everywhere, neither is it desirable to foster a culture where correct behaviour is dependent only on enforcement and penalties.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: It is better to also focus on education and awareness.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This is why LTA works with the community through Active Mobility Community Ambassadors to promote awareness of active mobility rules.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Members, such as Ms Gho Sze Kee, Ms Sylvia Lim and Ms Valerie Lee, asked about enforcement against unsafe devices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: LTA will act on feedback received via official channels and social media, surveillance as well as day-to-day operations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Targeted enforcement checks will also be conducted where e-scooters are commonly used, including areas where such devices may be parked or kept.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: PMDs verified by LTA as non-UL2272 certified will be seized.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: LTA has the responsibility to enforce against such devices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As Ms Sylvia Lim has acknowledged, LTA already conducts enforcement operations at residential areas to seize non-compliant active mobility devices and will continue to do so, working with our partners.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This Bill will allow us to go further.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: LTA can go beyond seizing the non-compliant device.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The individual can also be prosecuted for the offence of keeping the unsafe device.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This provides a stronger deterrent against fire hazards.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Cai Yinzhou and Ms Poh Li San asked about the disposal process for non-compliant devices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: If needed, owners may utilise designated e-waste recyclers or collection drives organised by ALBA in collaboration with Town Councils.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: They urged users to check that their devices meet safety standards and dispose of unsafe devices to keep their communities safe.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For PMAs, we may not expect to see a large-scale wave of disposals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To meet the new maximum device speed limit, many existing devices can simply be adjusted.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Those who do not qualify for a Certificate of Medical Need can resell their devices, provided they are compliant.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Disposal will likely be limited to oversized units or devices that cannot be brought into compliance, such as those with more than one seat, which are considered PMDs, which have their own set of requirements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Beyond the provisions in this Bill, Members have asked about other measures to reduce the fire risks of active mobility devices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I will touch on these briefly as we plan to address some of these issues in a subsequent Bill later this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Dr Hamid Razak asked for national guidelines for safe charging.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Cai Yinzhou suggested periodic inspections for PMAs in the absence of a mandated safety standard.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: While we continue to monitor the development of international standards for PMAs, LTA and the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) will remind the public of safe charging and usage practices when using motorised active mobility devices and against using modified second-hand devices and non-original parts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Dr Choo Pei Ling and Mr Cai Yinzhou asked how online marketplaces can take responsibility to eliminate unsafe and non-compliant devices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng suggested making it an offence for a seller to mislabel a device as compliant.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Since we commenced the Active Mobility Act, the sale of active mobility devices and related services are now more common online.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Due to time constraints, I have not addressed them all, but we will certainly study the points raised and continue to review how we implement the new laws in the Bill, as well as new measures needed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The proposals before us today represent more than new laws.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We want to restore the original purpose of PMAs and ensure that they serve those they were truly intended for and protect all path users at the same time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: With the Certificate of Medical Need, we distinguish genuine users from those who misuse mobility scooters.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Through registration of mobility scooters, we create accountability and ensure users purchase compliant devices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: By making it illegal to keep unsafe devices, we keep communities safer.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As we conclude this debate, let us return to the fundamental principle that path safety is not merely a regulatory matter.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: While this Bill covers PMAs and non-UL2272 certified PMDs, it is a collective responsibility by users of all device types and all path users that will define us as a gracious society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Like Ms Valerie Lee, my heart goes out to Mdm Mala who was hit by a PAB rider.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I have met her a few times in Tampines where she is a volunteer.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: But when I visited her in December at her home in Pasir Ris, she was unable to open her mouth.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Since then, her husband has been updating me and I am heartened that she is recovering slowly but steadily, and I wish her well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: It is these actions of the responsible majority that will keep paths safe and inclusive.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: And all of us can play a part.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: There were 24 speeches in total by fellow Members.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: I confess, my colleagues and I were not expecting this much interest in our Bill.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: But we are humbled and appreciative, because the speeches reflect how land transport is always top of mind for Singaporeans and there are many stakeholders and many points of view.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We have taken in Members’ feedback and suggestions to the best of our ability.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Senior Minister of State Sim Ann and Minister of State Baey Yam Keng have addressed the points raised on enforcement and on active mobility.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: I will round up the debate on points related to ERP 2.0 and other amendments covered in this Bill.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: For other topics that are not within the scope of this Bill, I would like to invite Members to consider filing Parliamentary Questions at future sessions.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: It is, in Dr Hamid’s words, a more mature regulatory approach.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Dr Choo asked whether shifting the onus for missed ERP payments to vehicle owners instead of the driver would create complications for shared vehicles.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: LTA has discussed these changes with fleet operators and taxi operators.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Today, vehicle owners are already responsible for obligations and fees such as road tax, so putting the responsibility of missed ERP payments on the owner would be consistent.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We expect vehicle owners, such as shared fleet owners to establish their own arrangements with the drivers to recover missed ERP payments, if necessary.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Dr Choo, Ms Tin Pei Ling, as well as Mr Melvin Yong also asked about plans for distance-based charging.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: I would like the transition to ERP 2.0 to be as smooth as possible.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: So, it is best to let the situation stabilise and to have motorists get used to the new system before too many parameters, or new ones, are introduced.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Distance-based charging is still an option for the future.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We have to study this further, as there are many trade-offs involved, as many Members have pointed out.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: But if we decide to implement distance-based charging, motorists will have ample notice.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Our desire to have a smooth transition is also why we are keeping the broad framework for ERP charges for now.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: The infrastructure light nature of ERP 2.0 does mean that we can more easily adjust locations where we can have road pricing.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Therefore, we can react more quickly to mitigate traffic congestion at hotspots, including in areas where it may not be physically possible to add an ERP 1.0 gantry today.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Mr Dennis Tan asked how we will manage ERP 2.0 data.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: This is a topic we have discussed before and have also discussed the use of Government data during the last Parliament Sitting, when we passed the Public Sector Governance Act.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: LTA adheres to all laws and Government-wide standards on data sharing with other agencies and this includes how we will manage ERP 2.0 data.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: As we have said before, LTA will use vehicle-specific data only for payment, charges and enforcement.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: And this will include non-payment of ERP charges and cross-border taxi enforcement.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: To prevent unauthorised access to the data, there are security measures and safeguards in place.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: For example, the design of the OBU is in line with the Federal Information Processing Standard level 4 security standard with cryptographic security keys.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Mr Edward Chia spoke extensively on how ERP 2.0 data can result in smarter traffic management and transport planning.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: LTA is indeed excited by this possibility, and we will use anonymised and aggregated ERP 2.0 data for traffic management and transport planning purposes For example, we are experimenting with merging or using this data to optimise the traffic light signal system, amongst other use cases that we are exploring.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: There is certainly great potential to improve traffic management using ERP 2.0 data.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: As we get better at doing so, it may well be feasible to create more capacity on our roads without taking up more land.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Potentially this can allow us to have some future growth in our car population.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: As we move closer to completing the transition to ERP 2.0, we are also addressing the final technical difficulties preventing some vehicles from installing OBUs.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: For instance, some electric vehicle models are unable to provide a constant power supply to the OBU.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: To overcome this, LTA has developed an External Battery Device to allow for the installation of OBUs for these vehicles.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Owners of such cars will then have to pay a daily flat fee if they use their vehicles on ERP operational days.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: On safety and enforcement, this House is aligned on the need for deterrence, accountability and proportionality.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: On active mobility, we want to strike the right balance: to preserve the independence and dignity that PMAs provide for those with genuine needs, but also to act firmly against misuse and dangerous behaviour that puts others in jeopardy.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: This Bill gives us the stronger tools to do so, and we will implement them with utmost care and consideration.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Mobility brings opportunity, but it must also come with responsibility.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: With the support of this House, this Bill will allow us to keep our transportation system safe, inclusive and ready for the future.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Clarification for the Minister, the Senior Minister of State and the Minister of State?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Looks like the round-up speeches by the three officeholders are very comprehensive.      .

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 5.05 pm.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended at 4.43 pm until 5.05 pm.
